items.title: Forecasting 'tipping points' with AI climate simulation
items.excerpt: Caltech, CU Boulder and NVIDIA researchers used a recurrent neural operator to forecast tipping points in simplified climate and wing-airflow simulations, predicting a simulated loss of ocean low clouds more than two years ahead with about 11 days of timing error (PNAS).

items.title: When simulations fall short, this spectrometer learns for itself
items.excerpt: Aarhus University researchers used AI to let an NMR spectrometer learn the best pulse sequence directly from the sample, instead of relying on simulations, to boost weak signals that limit what the instrument can see.

items.title: Rice plants can fight off devastating disease after gene editing with AI-designed tool
items.excerpt: University of Missouri researchers used an AI-designed genome-editing tool to create rice plants that resist bacterial blight, a disease that can destroy harvests across Asia and Africa.

items.title: AI may quickly generate ideas, but working with people leads to more creative ones
items.excerpt: A study comparing idea generation with generative AI versus human collaboration finds AI is faster but people working together produce more creative ideas.

items.title: 10 minutes is all it takes for AI assistance to erode your motivation, study shows
items.excerpt: In problem-solving experiments, people who used AI to get answers were more likely to give up and fail once that help was removed, compared with people who never used AI.

items.title: Is AI making you lazier?
items.excerpt: Following a study showing people who rely on AI for basic tasks like math became less motivated, Live Science polled readers on whether AI is eroding their effort and skills.

items.title: AI Proved the Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis. What Happens Now?
items.excerpt: Unlike other recent AI proofs, the AI-generated proof of the quasi-Riemann hypothesis has been unpacked by human experts, and one mathematician calls the implications 'staggering.'

items.title: Can we trust LLMs to judge whether a research idea is novel?
items.excerpt: Ai2's Old Ideas, Novel Problems benchmark tests how reliably LLMs judge the novelty of research ideas and finds small changes to the evaluation setup can flip their verdicts.

items.title: How researchers are adapting olmOCR 2 for historical and archaeological archives
items.excerpt: Researchers are adapting Ai2's open olmOCR 2 model to make historical photo libraries searchable locally and to improve transcription of handwritten archaeological records.

items.title: Accelerating the search for antimicrobial peptides with Google Antigravity
items.excerpt: Google DeepMind shows its Antigravity agentic platform acting as a science workbench that uses the ProtNLM model to scan millions of uncharacterized UniProt proteins and prioritize candidate antimicrobial peptides in a single session.

items.title: We'll pay to get revenge on an algorithm, even though it can't feel a thing
items.excerpt: In experiments with more than 6,000 participants, people sacrificed their own money to retaliate against unfair machine decisions, even though an algorithm cannot feel the loss.

items.title: Q&A: How AI came to model the 'messy' human mind
items.excerpt: MIT's Benjamin Lindquist discusses his research on how randomness and irrationality were built into early AI models designed to mimic human creativity.

items.title: Making machines that can listen
items.excerpt: MIT professor Paris Smaragdis works on machine listening so AI can hear and understand sounds the way humans do, improving artificial perception across applications.

items.title: To detect deepfake videos, researchers turn to the physics of light
items.excerpt: An optical technique for detecting deepfake videos claims 97.8% accuracy while using less energy than digital neural networks with similar performance.

items.title: A unified coarse-grained neural network potential for the dynamics of biomolecular complexes
items.excerpt: AMARO v2.0 is a coarse-grained neural network potential that keeps all heavy atoms and treats solvent implicitly, giving one shared representation for proteins, drug-like molecules and their complexes to reach rare events atomistic molecular dynamics struggles with.

items.title: Interspecies communication
items.excerpt: Machine learning now detects animal calls and identifies which individual made them, as with the Earth Species Project's work on carrion crows, and researchers think more advanced AI and LLM-style models could help decode animal communication.

items.title: Astrolab's upcoming rover will run the first LLMs on the moon
items.excerpt: Astrolab's FLIP rover will carry an onboard AI demonstration running large language models on the lunar surface, a step toward more autonomy in future space missions.

items.title: 'We were looking at it wrong': The explosive claim that's upended the AI world
items.excerpt: An exclusive interview with researcher Nick Cammarata, whose viral 26,000-word post argues LLM internals are less complicated than assumed, a claim reshaping interpretability research.

items.title: Pasqal Launches AI Workflow for Cloud Quantum Experiments
items.excerpt: Pasqal's new AI-driven cloud workflow prepares quantum jobs, validates them in emulation, and processes the results into scientific observables.
